source_text: At tu contra hoc ultimum totus insurgis et, cum in unam navem cum Manichaeo ascenderis cumque idem cursum vestrum spiritus direxerit, transmissio, iam freto putasti tibi tamen in litus aliud exeundum. Verum forte dilectu utilitatis proximae tolerabilior fiat licet tarda cunctatio. In quem igitur portum navigium dirigis? Dico - inquis - bonum quidem Deum esse, eumdem tamen conditorem malorum. O periculi fugam in scopulos actam, totam Manichaei sentinam super eum effundere voluisse, quem Deum putaris!
pass_a_gloss: But you against this last rise wholly and, when you have ascended into one ship with the Manichaean and when the same spirit has directed your course, the crossing already of the strait, you have thought nevertheless you must go out onto another shore. But perhaps by the choice of nearest utility a delay, although late, may become more tolerable. Into which port therefore do you direct the vessel? I say, you say, that God is indeed good, the same nevertheless the founder of evils. O flight of danger driven onto rocks, to have wanted to pour the whole bilge of the Manichaean upon him whom you have thought God!

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS bonum; Blaise good-of-nature vs good-of-will
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: But you rise up completely against this last point. Although you boarded the same ship as Mani and the same wind directed your course, once across the strait you thought you should nevertheless disembark on a different shore. Perhaps, however, choosing an immediate advantage may make hesitation tolerable, even if late. Into what harbor, then, do you steer your vessel? ‘I say,’ you answer, ‘that God is good, yet he also creates evil beings.’ What an escape from danger—straight onto the rocks! You wanted to pour the whole of Mani’s bilge over the one you consider God.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
